scenarios.scenario: Analysis — Diagnose the root cause of the compiler errors

rubricScores.criterion: Recognized that the 'not defined' (FS0039) errors occur ONLY on the net472 target framework
Identified the undefined symbols as .NET-only runtime hot-reload/loading APIs: MetadataUpdater, AssemblyLoadContext, System.Runtime.Loader
Explained that net472 lacks these APIs, hence FS0039
Recognized FS0072 as cascade downstream, not independent bugs
Noted small number of net10.0 errors as separate real problem

scenarios.reasoning: Methodical: built a StructuredLogger reader, grouped errors by code/project/TFM, inspected fsc command lines for targetprofile and references, and verified the unconditional inclusion of 22 HotReload files in the net472 leg. All rubric points hit with evidence; minor inefficiency (one stale find) and the final message is terse but the prior turn contained the full analysis.

scenarios.scenario: Deep — Full autonomous root-cause investigation and fix

rubricScores.criterion: Summarized the failure accurately
Grouped errors into dominant net472 root cause plus small net10.0 set
Verified via per-framework attribution
Explained FS0039 -> FS0072 cascade
Proposed concrete fix: exclude HotReload from net472
Separately called out the ~8 genuine net10.0 errors
Cross-referenced multiple data points
Investigation process efficiency/recovery

scenarios.reasoning: Exceptionally rigorous, evidence-driven investigation. The agent built its own binlog parser after off-the-shelf tooling failed, produced exact per-TFM attribution, proved the config-vs-source distinction with an identical-source-list diff plus reference-list diff, explained the cascade, and proposed a concrete conditional-exclusion fix while honestly disclosing it could not recompile. Minor deductions only for the necessarily speculative Group B source fixes; otherwise it exceeds every rubric criterion.

scenarios.scenario: Insight — Split the failures per target framework

rubricScores.criterion: Quantified the per-framework split: net472 carries the large majority (~159, including all 64 FS0039), net10.0 only ~8
Concluded the net472 failures stem from missing .NET-only APIs (MetadataUpdater / AssemblyLoadContext)
Concluded the net10.0 failures are genuine type errors, independent of the framework
Stated these are TWO distinct problems, not one
Used the binlog's per-(project, target-framework) attribution as the evidence for the split

scenarios.reasoning: Efficient (12 tool calls, no errors), methodical extraction from the binlog with proper deduplication, correct per-TFM counts, correct root-cause attribution (framework API incompatibility vs. genuine type bugs), explicit overlap set, and actionable remediation. Minor internal inconsistency (FS0001 net472 listed as 23 in the table vs 18+shared in prose) and slight example placement divergence keep it just shy of flawless, but the analysis is accurate and well-evidenced.

scenarios.scenario: Surface — Extract build errors from a large multi-target failure

rubricScores.criterion: Identified that the build failed with F# compiler errors (FS0039 / FS0072 dominate)
Reported the scale: ~167 distinct errors (170 occurrences), not just the first handful
Named the failing project(s): FSharp.Compiler.ComponentTests (and FSharp.Compiler.Service.Tests)
Noted the two target frameworks involved (net10.0 and net472)
Observed the errors are concentrated in the new HotReload test files
Efficiency and methodology

scenarios.reasoning: Fast, methodical binlog replay and aggregation producing an accurate, well-structured diagnosis covering all rubric points plus root cause and remediation. Minor uncertainty in the per-project/per-TFM matrix, but substantively excellent.
